data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 reduces to SRC_001: the claim that algorithmic convergence on shared training data makes decentralized networks strictly less resilient is a specific instance of the observer-bias artifact, because the shared training data is a heavy-tailed catastrophic shared cause whose correlated failure signal is fragmented across isolated operators and never recognized. The reduction is refuted if regulatory or systemic monitoring forces centralized reporting of small operator failures, making the shared training data correlation visible and the resilience artifact disappear, or if small services use private, non-shared training data, eliminating the shared cause.
